Definition: Understandability refers to how easily developers can comprehend and maintain the test code.

Task: Improve the understandability of the test `JaroWinklerSimilarityTest.java` (path:- /Users/tenghaha/Projects/New_Agent_understandability_improvement/local_workplace/commons-text/src/test/java/org/apache/commons/text/similarity/JaroWinklerSimilarityTest.java). The refactored code must be syntactically correct and compilable against the provided CUT signatures. Do not alter the runtime behaviour of the original test: the same methods must be called with the same arguments and produce the same expected outcomes.

I have a clear picture. Both big test methods exercise the **same** set of input pairs and expected scores — they differ only in how the inputs are constructed (`SimilarityInputTest.build` vs. `wrap`/`String`). The main understandability problems are the large blocks of near-identical magic-number assertions and the unexplained tighter delta on the `"fly"/"ant"` case.

I'll extract the shared cases into one named, documented table and have both tests iterate it — preserving every `apply` call, argument, expected value, and delta exactly.Compiles cleanly (`COMPILE_OK`). I refactored the two large duplicated assertion blocks into one documented `SIMILARITY_CASES` table iterated by both tests, named the two delta values (`DELTA` and `EXACT_ZERO_DELTA`) with explanations, and added descriptive failure messages — all while preserving the exact `apply` calls, arguments, expected scores, and tolerances.
